admission_record: Sex: male. Age: 76 years. Marital status: married. The patient presented with sudden left-sided limb weakness for 19 hours. He was found after a fall at 16:00 on the previous day, remained conscious, and had no convulsions or incontinence. His left arm and leg were weak and he required assistance to walk. The last-known-well time was 16:00. At first contact the following morning, blood pressure was 144/88 mmHg and GCS was 15. His prestroke mRS was 0. Medical history included hypertension for 20 years and atrial fibrillation or valvular heart disease. There was no prior stroke, TIA, intracranial hemorrhage, recent surgery, trauma, or known bleeding tendency. He was not taking antiplatelet or anticoagulant medication.
neuro_exam: The patient was alert and cooperative, with slurred speech and a shallow left nasolabial fold. Strength was grade IV in the left arm and leg and grade V on the right. Sensation and coordination were preserved, and the left pathological reflex was positive. The recorded admission NIHSS was 9.
chief_complaint: Left-sided limb weakness with slurred speech for 19 hours.
fact_content: Key facts: 76-year-old man with sudden left-sided limb weakness beginning approximately 19 hours before presentation; last known well at 16:00 on the previous day; prestroke mRS 0; admission NIHSS 9; history of hypertension and atrial fibrillation or valvular heart disease; no prior stroke, TIA, recent surgery, trauma, or known bleeding tendency; no antiplatelet or anticoagulant medication before admission.
